quarantine.statement: This script never opens, reads, scores, globs, tunes or diagnoses on the quarantined fixtures; _assert_quarantine() greps this source and aborts if any of those names ever sits next to open( / load( / glob( / read_ / Path(. The persona4 figure (23/36 = 63.9% top-1) is a handed-down constant, never recomputed.
quarantine.scope_of_that_claim: It covers THIS SCRIPT only. Reads by other processes in the same session are listed in known_reads_this_session; an unchanged atime does NOT rule them out on this volume.

known_reads_this_session.why: library proper-noun hygiene audit -- reads the fixture for vocabulary; runs on every pytest invocation. Not a scoring, tuning or diagnostic read, but it IS a read.
non-modification witness recorded in the report; reads bytes, extracts no content and no sample-level information

stat_only_timestamps._witness_note: size+mtime+ctime are the NON-MODIFICATION witness: ctime advances on any content or metadata change and cannot be backdated by touch(1). atime is recorded for completeness but is NOT a read witness on this volume -- a controlled probe in scratch/refound showed reads leaving atime unchanged, so an unchanged atime proves nothing about reads.

read_barrier.how: quarantine_guard.enforce() wraps builtins.open, io.open, os.open and numpy.load; a quarantined path raises QuarantineViolation. Installed as the FIRST statement of main(), before any fixture is loaded.

shipped_tagger_fidelity.note: correct = entities_match against the fixture's ground-truth attribute label; the oracle arms replace exactly these two functions with the ground truth.

query_tagger_dose_response.arm: gold write gate, shipped direction inference, PERFECT doc tags, conversational docs and queries; f = fraction of DISTINCT question phrasings whose query_intent is replaced by the ground truth
query_tagger_dose_response.note: fraction_of_questions_tagged is MEASURED, not assumed, and is what f* is solved against. The head_only pool never tags a question whose attribute head is absent from the text -- it is the only pool a query-text tagger could actually reach.

phrasing_ladder_shipped_build.arm: gold write gate, shipped direction inference, shipped tagger, conversational multi-fact documents; ONLY the question wording changes

decision.verdict: (ii) NOT ACHIEVABLE FROM THE QUERY TEXT -- the achievable ceiling is 66.4% [61.8, 70.8], 13.6 points BELOW the 80.0% target, and the whole interval is below it. Reaching 80.0% additionally requires tagging questions whose attribute head is ABSENT from the text (the ANNOTATION ceiling, 89.5%), which no tagger can read off the query.

oracle_tag_validity.question: an oracle QUERY tag names the ATTRIBUTE, not the document. If the attribute group held one document the tag would hand over the answer and the ceiling would be an artefact.

half_oracle_artefact.question: Does giving DOCUMENTS ground-truth tags, while the shipped tagger still reads the head-dropped QUESTIONS, penalise those questions? If so the achievable ceiling understates.
half_oracle_artefact.population: the 182 head-dropped questions, which no ACHIEVABLE arm tags
half_oracle_artefact.verdict: NO PENALTY on this set: oracle document tags move the un-oracled questions +2.2 points, and the full achievable stack moves them +5.5. The achievable ceiling is NOT deflated by the half-oracle, so the 66.4% figure is not a loose lower bound.

contrast_temporal_bench_native.note: On temporal_bench's NATIVE templated shape the same construction costs a lot, because its questions use registry vocabulary that the shipped tagger already matches, so replacing the document side breaks a match that was working. On conversational chat questions there is no such match to break. That is why the T2 row must not be read as a result about tagging, and why the chat artefact had to be measured separately rather than inferred from it.

restated_target.reason: The achievable ceiling is 66.4% [61.8, 70.8] -- 13.6 points BELOW the 80.0% target, whole interval below it. The target is NOT reachable from the query text on this set, however good the tagger or the ranking layer gets, because 43.3% of questions do not contain their attribute head at all. The 89.5% ANNOTATION ceiling that does clear the target is reached only by handing the engine a label the query does not carry. Either the LEVEL moves to the achievable ceiling, or the SHAPE of the question distribution moves (canonicalise, or ask the user to name the attribute), or the engine gets a source of attribute identity other than the query text -- conversation context, which nothing in this study measured.
specification_fixes: name the ARM: gold_stores, not end_to_end -- they differ by 15.2 points [8.6, 21.9] on this set
n >= 246 questions, so the 95% Wilson half-width at p=0.80 is <= 5 points (at n=36 it is ~12)
score the declared TEST split only; dev is for tuning
gate on the 95 percent Wilson LOWER bound >= 75, not the point estimate

level_recommendation.suggested: If the level must stay 80%, the SET has to change: a question distribution whose head-drop rate is low enough for 80% to be reachable. On this set the achievable ceiling is 66.4% at a 43.3% head-drop rate, and the shipped build already scores 84.3% [80.5, 87.5] when questions name the attribute. If the SET stays as it is, the defensible gold-store top-1 level is at most the achievable ceiling 66.4%, not 80%.

mechanism_gate.statement: Moving BOTH ends of the entity chain to PERFECT reaches 66.4% [61.8, 70.8], which is 13.6 points short of 80.0%. Both ends are necessary and together they are NOT sufficient: the rest of the gap is questions that never name their attribute.
mechanism_gate.query_intent_accuracy_needed_pct_note: that figure comes from the all_texts dose curve, which is allowed to tag phrasings with no attribute head in them. Restricted to the phrasings a tagger can actually read, the curve saturates at 65.0% and NEVER reaches 80.0% -- so this is a requirement on annotation, not on a tagger.
mechanism_gate.query_intent_accuracy_needed_pct_ACHIEVA: unreachable: the head-surviving dose curve saturates at 65.0%

cheaper_alternative_if_the_level_must_be.route: change the TASK, not the engine: canonicalise the question to an attribute head before ranking, or ask the user to name the attribute
cheaper_alternative_if_the_level_must_be.caveat: this is not the deployment shape; it is a different task

oracle_leak_audit.rule: An 'achievable' arm may tag ONLY questions whose attribute head survives the phrasing it asks.  head_dropped_questions_tagged must be 0 on every such arm; the run aborts otherwise.
